classification.difficultyReason: Calculate square, rectangular and triangular base areas before applying the pyramid volume formula; distinguish base altitude from pyramid height.

content.prompt: Calculate the volume of each pyramid.

spec.description: Square-based pyramid with matching double ticks on adjacent base edges, a 10 cm side label and the statement height = 12 cm. Ordinary outlines and hidden edges use black; dashes retain visibility information.
spec.mathematics: Square base side 10 cm; perpendicular pyramid height 12 cm.

spec.description: Rectangular-based pyramid with 8 cm front edge, 5 cm receding edge and an external vertical 4 cm height dimension with dotted projection guides.
spec.mathematics: Rectangular base 8 cm by 5 cm; perpendicular pyramid height 4 cm.

spec.description: Triangular-based pyramid with perpendicular 6 cm and 8 cm base edges. External vertical 10 cm height dimension and dotted projection guides; the remaining base edge is dashed.
spec.mathematics: Right-triangular base with perpendicular sides 6 cm and 8 cm; pyramid height 10 cm.

spec.description: Triangular-based pyramid with 12 cm front base edge, dashed base altitude, right-angle mark and external 6 cm dimension parallel to that altitude. The separate statement height = 8 cm gives the pyramid height.
spec.mathematics: Triangular base area is one half times 12 cm times its 6 cm altitude. Perpendicular pyramid height is 8 cm.

answer.worked:
The $6\text{ cm}$ measurement is the altitude of the triangular base; the pyramid height is $8\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\times12\times6\\A&=36\text{ cm}^2\\V&=\frac13Ah\\V&=\frac13\times36\times8\\V&=96\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$

teachingContext.methodNote: Find the base area, then substitute the perpendicular pyramid height into V = one third × base area × height, as in Example 4.
teachingContext.mappingNote: All four parts directly assess pyramid volume; parts c and d additionally require the area of a triangular base.
